reply.english: The weather's nice, the sun's out.

reply.arabic: مَا عَرْفْتِش، وَلَكِن الْجَو غَايِم شْوِيَّة
reply.english: I don't know, but it's a bit cloudy.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير يوسف، كيفاش الجو اليوم؟
dialogue.transliteration: Sbaa7 lkheer Youssef, kifash ljaw lyoom?
dialogue.english: Good morning Youssef, what's the weather like today?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور. الجو غايم شوية، ولكن ما كاينش البرد
dialogue.transliteration: Sbaa7 nnoor. ljaw ghaayem shwiya, walakin ma kaynsh lberd
dialogue.english: Good morning. It's a bit cloudy, but it isn't cold.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: واش كتظن غادي تشتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: waash kteDenn ghaadi teshti?
dialogue.english: Do you think it's going to rain?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: ما عرفتش، ولكن كاين الريح بزاف من الصباح
dialogue.transliteration: ma 3reftsh, walakin kayn rreeh bzaaf mn SSbaa7
dialogue.english: I don't know, but there's been a lot of wind since morning.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: أنا حاسة بلي الدنيا سخونة كتر من البارح
dialogue.transliteration: ana 7aassa bli ddenya skhoona ktar mn lbaare7
dialogue.english: I feel like it's hotter than yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: لا، أنا حاس بالعكس، الجو برد شوية
dialogue.transliteration: la, ana 7aass bl3aks, ljaw berd shwiya
dialogue.english: No, I feel the opposite, it's gotten a bit colder.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: المهم، شفتي الشمس طالعة؟
dialogue.transliteration: lmohimm, shefti shshems Taal3a?
dialogue.english: Anyway, did you see the sun's out?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: إيه، ولكن الغيم مغطيها شوية
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, walakin lgheem mghaTTeeha shwiya
dialogue.english: Yes, but the clouds are covering it a bit.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: خود معاك الشمسية على كل حال
dialogue.transliteration: khood m3aak shshemsiya 3la kull 7aal
dialogue.english: Take an umbrella with you anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مزيان بلي فكرتيني
dialogue.transliteration: mzyaan bli fekkertini
dialogue.english: Good thing you reminded me.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: بالسلامة، نشوفك من بعد إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: bssalaama, nshoofek mn b3ed in shaa2 Allah
dialogue.english: Bye, see you later God willing.

response.english: It's hot and the sun's out.

pair.english: Do I need to take the umbrella?

response.english: Yes, because it's going to rain.

lessons.culture: In Morocco the weather is an easy opener with anyone, and rain is usually welcomed with "الحمد لله" or "الله يجعلها شتا خير" because water matters. In Casablanca and Rabat the Atlantic brings damp air and cloud, so "غايم" and "الرطوبة" come up often.

phrases.english: In winter it gets very cold in Rabat.

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: كريم، أشمن فصل كيعجبك؟
dialogue.transliteration: Kareem, ashmen faSl kay3jbek?
dialogue.english: Karim, which season do you like?

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: كنحب الصيف، حيت كنمشي للبحر مع العائلة
dialogue.transliteration: kan7ebb SSeef, 7eet kanmshi lel b7er m3a l3aa2ila
dialogue.english: I love summer, because I go to the sea with the family.

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: أنا لا، الصيف فالدار البيضاء طويل والجو كيكون رطب بزاف
dialogue.transliteration: ana la, SSeef fddaar lbeyDa Taweel w ljaw kaykoon rTeb bzaaf
dialogue.english: Not me, summer in Casablanca is long and it gets very humid.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: عندك الحق، ولكن فالشتا كيكون البرد بزاف
dialogue.transliteration: 3ndek l7eqq, walakin fshshta kaykoon lberd bzaaf
dialogue.english: You're right, but in winter it gets very cold.

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: أنا كنفضل الربيع، كتعجبني ريحة الشتا فالربيع
dialogue.transliteration: ana kanfeDDel rrbee3, kat3jebni ree7t shshta frrbee3
dialogue.english: I prefer spring, I like the smell of rain in spring.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: وفالخريف؟ الورق كيطيح من الشجرة والجو كيتبدل
dialogue.transliteration: w flkhreef? lwerq kayTee7 mn shshejra w ljaw kaytbeddel
dialogue.english: And fall? The leaves fall from the trees and the weather changes.

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: إيه، الجو كيتبدل بزاف بين الفصول
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, ljaw kaytbeddel bzaaf been lfSool
dialogue.english: Yes, the weather changes a lot between the seasons.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: واش شفتي التلج فالجبل هاد العام؟
dialogue.transliteration: waash shefti ttelj fljbel haad l3aam?
dialogue.english: Have you seen the snow on the mountain this year?

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: إيه، كيطيح التلج فالجبل فالشتا، وكنمشيو نتفرجو عليه
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, kayTee7 ttelj fljbel fshshta, w kanmshiw ntferrjo 3leeh
dialogue.english: Yes, snow falls on the mountain in winter and we go to look at it.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: زوين بزاف. فالشتا خاصك تلبس حوايج تقال
dialogue.transliteration: zween bzaaf. fshshta khaSSek telbes 7waayej teqaal
dialogue.english: Lovely. In winter you need to wear heavy clothes.

dialogue.speaker: Amina
dialogue.arabic: صافي، غادي نلبس التريكو ونبقى فالدار
dialogue.transliteration: Saafi, ghaadi nelbes ttreeko w nbqa fddaar
dialogue.english: Alright, I'll wear a sweater and stay home.

pair.english: What's the weather like in winter?

lessons.culture: In Darija "الشتا" means both rain and winter, so context tells you which. Snow is not something Casablanca or Rabat see, so families drive to Ifrane or the Middle Atlas to see it, and in summer the beaches and the corniche fill up.

lessons.culture: Casablanca and Rabat winters are damp and cool, so people dress in layers, and the djellaba with its hood is a warm everyday outer layer for many, men and women alike. In summer the strong Atlantic sun makes hats and sunglasses common.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: عمر، إلا كان الجو زوين غدا، نخرجو للحديقة؟
dialogue.transliteration: 3omar, ila kaan ljaw zween ghedda, nkhrjo lel 7adeeqa?
dialogue.english: Omar, if the weather's nice tomorrow, shall we go out to the park?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: يلا، ولكن واش شفتي الميتيو؟
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, walakin waash shefti lmeteeyo?
dialogue.english: Sure, but did you see the forecast?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: لا، ما شفتوش
dialogue.transliteration: la, ma sheftoosh
dialogue.english: No, I didn't see it.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كيقولو غادي تشتي غدا فالعشية
dialogue.transliteration: kayqoolo ghaadi teshti ghedda fl3eshiya
dialogue.english: They say it's going to rain tomorrow afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: إلا شتات، نأجلو الخرجة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ila shtaat, n2ajjlo lkhorja?
dialogue.english: If it rains, shall we postpone the outing?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: إيه، نأجلوها لنهار الأحد إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, n2ajjloha lnhaar l7ed in shaa2 Allah
dialogue.english: Yes, we'll postpone it to Sunday God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: وشنو كتقول نبقاو فالدار غدا؟
dialogue.transliteration: w shnoo ktqool nbqaaw fddaar ghedda?
dialogue.english: And what do you say to staying home tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: صافي، ولكن الليلة الجو مزيان، نقعدو فالبلكون؟
dialogue.transliteration: Saafi, walakin llila ljaw mzyaan, nq3do flbalkoon?
dialogue.english: Fine, but tonight the weather's pleasant, shall we sit on the balcony?

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: يلا، غادي نحضر الأتاي
dialogue.transliteration: yalla, ghaadi n7eDDer latay
dialogue.english: Yes, I'll make the tea.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: والرحلة للجبل نهار السبت على حساب الجو
dialogue.transliteration: w rre7la lljbel nhaar ssbt 3la 7saab ljaw
dialogue.english: And the trip to the mountain on Saturday depends on the weather.

dialogue.speaker: Sara
dialogue.arabic: إن شاء الله يكون الجو زوين
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2 Allah ykoon ljaw zween
dialogue.english: God willing the weather will be nice.

pair.english: Shall we go out to the park today?

response.english: Yes, it's going to rain tomorrow.
Yes, until the weather gets better.

lessons.culture: Plans in Morocco lean on the weather, and "إن شاء الله" is added to almost any plan for tomorrow. In Rabat people walk along the Bouregreg and the Oudayas, and in Casablanca along the corniche, but a rainy or foggy day usually means postponing, not cancelling, and many check "الميتيو" on their phone first.

lessons.culture: Rain is a blessing in Morocco after dry years: when it comes people say "الحمد لله" and "الله يكثّر الخير", and when it is late mosques hold صلاة الاستسقاء, the prayer for rain. Heavy autumn storms flood low streets in Casablanca and cut the power ("تقطع الضو"), so people stay home until it passes. "الحمد لله" is the shared Islamic formula, said the same in every dialect.

lessons.culture: Moroccans call the forecast "الميتيو", from French météo, and check it on the phone or in the bulletin after the evening news, which gives the highest and lowest temperature city by city. challenge.title: Plan Your Day Around the Weather
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Moroccan Darija conversation, at least 10 lines, between two friends deciding what to do today based on the weather. It must include asking about the weather, describing the weather with at least two different weather words, a mention of the season, advice on what to wear, and a decision on whether to go out or stay home.
required_elements: A question asking what the weather is like, using كيفاش الجو.
At least two different weather descriptions, such as سخون, بارد, غايم, or كتشتي.
A mention of the season, using a word like الصيف, الشتا, الربيع, or الخريف.
Advice on what to wear, using خاصك تلبس or لبس.
A condition using إلا كان الجو زوين or الجو ماشي زوين.
A line using خود معاك الشمسية or a similar reminder.
A final decision to go out (نخرجو) or stay home (نبقاو فالدار).
